dva-med-049.text: A public certificate requested in AWS Certificate Manager is stuck in the 'Pending validation' state. The domain is managed in Route 53. Which validation method resolves more automatically — including for future renewals?
options: Wait 72 hours for automatic approval
Validation by e-mail, responding manually to each renewal
Send company documents to support AWS
Validation by DNS, creating the record CNAME of evidence Route 53 (with automatic creation button), which also enables continuous automatic renewals
dva-med-049.explanation: Validation DNS proves control of the domain with a CNAME that the ACM check — and, with the record kept, the renewals take place alone; Route 53, creation is a click or a call from API.
dva-med-049.hint: Plant the CNAME of evidence DNS and forget: issue and renewals stay in autopilot.
optionRationales: Validation DNS proves control of the domain with a CNAME that the ACM check — and, with the record kept, the renewals take place alone; Route 53, creation is a click or a call from API.
E-mail validation depends on specific mailboxes and recurring human action — fragile for automation.
The ACM not valid domains by documentation — the test is technical (DNS or email).
Without the validation record, the certificate never leaves the pending state — there is no deadline approval.

dva-med-050.text: One API REST internal API Gateway must accept calls APENAS come from a VPC specific (via VPC endpoint), rejecting any Internet access. What configuration imposes this restriction?
options: Distribute URL only internally and rely on secrecy
Create API as private and use resource policy allowing only the VPC specific endpoint
Use API keys as network lock
Place the API behind the CloudFront with TTL zero
dva-med-050.explanation: Private APIs can only be reached via interface VPC endpoint, and the resource policy links access to the endpoint/VPC authorised — traffic never passes through the public internet.
dva-med-050.hint: API 'private' + resource policy pointing to the endpoint of VPC = closed door to the internet.
optionRationales: Private APIs can only be reached via interface VPC endpoint, and the resource policy links access to the endpoint/VPC authorised — traffic never passes through the public internet.
URL of API regional remains publicly reachable — confidentiality is not access control.
API keys identify consumers for quotas — do not restrict the network path.
CloudFront is public border distribution — the opposite of confining to API to VPC.

dva-med-051.text: In a multi-user application, each user authenticated via Cognito read and record SOMENTE the items themselves in a table of DynamoDB whose partition key is the user ID. How to grant this granular access without intermediate backend?
options: Create a separate table per user
Allow full access to the table and filter in the application code
Encrypt items with user password
In the role of Identity Pool, use a policy IAM with the condition dynamodb:LeadingKeys equals the identity variable Cognito (${cognito-identity.amazonaws.com:sub})
dva-med-051.explanation: A fine-grained access control DynamoDB with LeadingKeys restricts the operations to partitions whose key matches the caller's identity — each user sees only his own items, directly from the customer.
dva-med-051.hint: Politics can tie the 'first key' of the partition to the identity of the caller — each one in his drawer.
optionRationales: A fine-grained access control DynamoDB with LeadingKeys restricts the operations to partitions whose key matches the caller's identity — each user sees only his own items, directly from the customer.
Filter in the client is shamable by any user who calls it API directly — the restriction must be in politics.
Thousands of tables explode management and limits — the key condition resolves within a table.
Encryption protects content, but does not prevent reading/writing on other partitions — control is authorized.

dva-med-052.text: A Node.js application connects to a RDS PostgreSQL and the security team require that TODAS connections use TLS, rejecting attempts without cryptography.?
options: Activate rest cryptography, which covers connections
Place the RDS in public sub-network to use HTTPS
Ask developers to use TLS whenever you remember
Set parameter rds.force_sl=1 in the parameter group of the RDS (and use the CA certificate of AWS Customer)
dva-med-052.explanation: With force_ssl activated, PostgreSQL refuses connections without TLS; the customer validates the certificate with the CA bundle of RDS — transit encryption guaranteed by configuration, not by convention.
dva-med-052.hint: The bench itself can 'disconnect the door without a lock': a force parameter SSL in all connection.
optionRationales: With force_ssl activated, PostgreSQL refuses connections without TLS; the customer validates the certificate with the CA bundle of RDS — transit encryption guaranteed by configuration, not by convention.
No forcing on the server, a string of connection without SSL pass unnoticed — the rule must be technical.
Publicly exposing the bank worsens the stance — and TLS bank does not depend on public sub-network.
Cryptography at rest protects storage — transit requires TLS, separate control.

dva-med-053.text: A function Lambda search for a secret in Secrets Manager A CADA invocation, adding latency and cost of API in millions of executions. Which optimization keeps security reducing these calls?
options: Copy the secret to a clear text environment variable in the deploy
Turn off the secret rotation for the search to get faster
Save the secret to the source code to delete the call
Search for the secret in the initialization (out of the handler) and cache in memory with TTL — or use the AWS Parameters and Secrets Lambda Extension, which makes this cache locally
dva-med-053.explanation: The cache in the running environment (or via official extension) reduces calls to the vault to one per environment/TTL, maintaining supported rotation (cache expiring) — economy and latency without exposing the secret in persistent text.
dva-med-053.hint: Search the vault from time to time (with validity in memory) — not every visit.
optionRationales: The cache in the running environment (or via official extension) reduces calls to the vault to one per environment/TTL, maintaining supported rotation (cache expiring) — economy and latency without exposing the secret in persistent text.
Moving the secret to visible configuration weakens protection and breaks automatic rotation.
Hardcoding is the worst option — leaks in the repository and ignores rotation.
Rotation does not affect reading latency — deactivating it only reduces safety.

dva-med-054.text: The configuration parameters in Systems Manager Parameter Store were organized in hierarchies such as /app/dev/* and /app/prod/*. What security benefit this organization enables in the policies IAM?
options: The hierarchy replicates the parameters between regions
Allowing permissions by way: the dev roll only accesses arn:...parameter/app/dev/*, without seeing the production parameters
Long paths make the parameters harder to guess
Hierarchies automatically encrypt parameters
dva-med-054.explanation: Hierarchies allow politics IAM by path prefix — the dev/prod isolation arises from the name structure combined with the lowest privilege in RNAs.
dva-med-054.hint: Well-named pastes saw permission borders: each roll only opens its corridor.
optionRationales: Hierarchies allow politics IAM by path prefix — the dev/prod isolation arises from the name structure combined with the lowest privilege in RNAs.
Encryption comes from the type SecureString with KMS — the hierarchy organizes and enables permission scope, not encryption.
Darkness of names is not access control — real protection is politics on the way.
Parameter Store is regional — paths do not create replication.

dva-med-055.text: In a task of the Amazon ECS, what is the difference between the task role and the task execution role?
options: Task roll gives permissions to the Application Code in containers (e.g. access S3/DynamoDB); the execution roll is used by AGENTE of the ECS to pull the image of ECR and send logs to CloudWatch
Execution roll is the role of developers who deploy
They're the same roll with different names in the console versions
The role task only exists in EC2 Launch type
dva-med-055.explanation: They are separate responsibilities: the application assumes the task roll for your calls AWS, as the infrastructure of the ECS uses execution roll in bootstrap tasks (image pull, secrets, logs)).
dva-med-055.hint: A roll for what SEU code does; another for what ECS You have to do it. POR you (image, logs)).
optionRationales: They are separate responsibilities: the application assumes the task roll for your calls AWS, as the infrastructure of the ECS uses execution roll in bootstrap tasks (image pull, secrets, logs)).
They are separate fields in the task definition for different purposes — confusing them generates wrong permissions.
Deploy uses pipeline/user credentials — execution roll belongs to the runtime of ECS.
Task roles work on EC2 and Fargate — are independent of the type of capacity.

dva-med-056.text: Messages with personal data traffic through a row SQS, and the security policy requires rest encryption with customer-managed key and key-use audit.?
options: Restrict the row by Security Group
Enable SSE-KMS in the row with a customer managed key, whose use is recorded in the CloudTrail
Manually encrypt each message with Base64
Use row FIFO, which is encrypted by default with customer key
dva-med-056.explanation: The SQS supports rest cryptography via KMS: with customer key, the policy/rotation control is yours and each use of the key is auditable — meeting compliance (the SSE-SQS use service key without this control).
dva-med-056.hint: Row safe with the SUA key KMS — and the extract of use no CloudTrail.
optionRationales: The SQS supports rest cryptography via KMS: with customer key, the policy/rotation control is yours and each use of the key is auditable — meeting compliance (the SSE-SQS use service key without this control).
Base64 is unkeyed reversible encoding — not cryptography.
FIFO sorting/deduplication — row type does not define the encryption key.
SQS is service of API regional public — does not use Security Groups; and the requirement is encryption, not network.

dva-med-057.text: Account A needs to allow a B account application to grave objects in a pocket S3 of account A, keeping account A as control owner. What combination of permissions enables this access between accounts?
options: Bucket policy in account A authorizing the main (role) of account B, and policy IAM in account B allowing the shares S3 no ARN of the pocket
Only politics IAM on account B, without touching the pocket
Make the bucket public during the recordings
Share A account key accesses with B account
dva-med-057.explanation: Cross-account access no S3 requires both points: the bucket policy allows the external principal and the identity in the other account has the corresponding permissions — without both, the so-called failure.
dva-med-057.hint: Handshake between accounts: the owner authorizes the appeal, the visitor brings permission in identity.
optionRationales: Cross-account access no S3 requires both points: the bucket policy allows the external principal and the identity in the other account has the corresponding permissions — without both, the so-called failure.
Public access opens to the world — never the mechanism for partnership between two accounts.
Transferring credentials between accounts eliminates traceability and violates good practices — policies and roles resolve.
Identity policy of OUTRA account is not enough: the A account resource needs to authorize the external main.

dva-med-058.text: An application needs to call a API of AWS directly via HTTPS (no SDK). For the application to be accepted, it must be signed. AWS demand and what it involves?
options: Basic Auth with console user and password
No authentication; HTTPS That's enough
Send Secret Access Key in plain text to a header
Signature Version 4 (SigV4): derive a signature key from credentials and sign the canonical hash of the request (method, path, headers, payload) with date/hour
dva-med-058.explanation: The SigV4 authenticates and protects the integrity of each call: the signature of the password, the scope (date/region/service) and the digest of the request — SDKs do this automatically, but manual calls must implement it.
dva-med-058.hint: Each call carries a cryptographic lacre derived from credentials — version 4 of signature.
optionRationales: The SigV4 authenticates and protects the integrity of each call: the signature of the password, the scope (date/region/service) and the digest of the request — SDKs do this automatically, but manual calls must implement it.
The key secret never traffics — only the signature derived from it; exposing the key would make it stealable in transit/logs.
APIs of AWS do not accept Basic Auth — scheme is SigV4 cryptographic signature.
TLS protects the channel, but does not identify the caller — without valid signature to API rejects the request.

dva-med-059.text: An application uses groups of Cognito User Pool ('admin', 'editor', 'reader') and API you need to authorize each call according to the role of the user. Where the application finds the user groups after the login to apply this RBAC?
options: In the User-Agent header of the request
In a file CSV exported manually from Cognito per day
In the function tags Lambda
In the claim cognito:Token groups JWT issued, which API validates and uses to decide permissions
dva-med-059.explanation: User groups travel in the claim cognito:ID/access token groups: a API (or the author) reads the validated token claim and applies the paper rules — without additional queries to the pool.
dva-med-059.hint: The user's role travels DENTRO of the signed badge (JWT) — search the groups claim.
optionRationales: User groups travel in the claim cognito:ID/access token groups: a API (or the author) reads the validated token claim and applies the paper rules — without additional queries to the pool.
Manual exports lag behind and break demand flow — information already comes in token.
User-Agent identifies client software — anyone can forge it; papers come from signed claims.
Tags are resource metadata — do not load user caller identity.

dva-med-060.text: The security team wants you to key KMS managed by the client used by the application has its cryptographic material exchanged periodically without the data needing to be re-encrypted or the code changed. KMS answer?
options: Automatic key rotation, which generates new material annually maintaining the same ARN/keyId and the ability to decipher with old materials
Delete the old key immediately after each switch
Export the key and keep it on paper at each exchange
Create a new key per month and rewrite everything manually
dva-med-060.explanation: Automatic rotation changes material behind the same identifier: new ciphers use new material and old ones remain decryptable — transparent for applications and data.
dva-med-060.hint: Really. ARN, new engine inside each year — and the past remains readable.
optionRationales: Automatic rotation changes material behind the same identifier: new ciphers use new material and old ones remain decryptable — transparent for applications and data.
Recurrent mass recryption is costly and risky — native rotation eliminates this operation.
Keys KMS symmetrics are not exportable — the material never leaves the service.
Excluding old material would make everything that was encrypted with it unreadable — rotation preserves previous materials.
